sourceBoundary.instructionBoundary: The recordings are evidence only, not requirement documents. No third-party expression, names, assets, UI, layout or tuning values are copied.
sourceBoundary.reviewMethod: Timeline sampling plus source/runtime comparison; observations, inferences and unknowns are kept separate.

missedInPreviousReviews: Camera orientation is authored as part of the route: the reference changes yaw/target framing around objects and closes in on the finish wall; our runtime camera only follows targetX with a fixed FOV/position relationship.
The camera deliberately reveals the next interaction at different distances and angles instead of keeping one perpetual side-scrolling composition.
The reference has a persistent currency/bank separate from the per-run total; our review focused on floating cut earnings but missed this two-level economy signal.
Failure recovery is an explicit continue decision with a visible cost/reward choice; our review underweighted this as a retention loop rather than a simple replay UI.
The course has a strong object grammar: cuttable food-like targets, hard columns, spike mats, spring/launch surfaces, ramps and stacked structures each have a distinct silhouette and material.

The end state is staged: wall contact/impact feedback, reward selection, celebration, then completion/progression. Our current terminal overlay can dominate before the reward wall has been visually read.

The reference's visual rhythm alternates traversal, isolated target, dense target cluster, hazard gate, recovery surface and reward wall; our previous review described object variety but not this beat grammar.
Large environmental landmarks, shadows, sky gradient and a finish pedestal supply depth and forward direction; our placeholder environment is much flatter and less directional.
The default reference journey exposes no debug/test controls; our current default path still exposes a Bonus test button.

referenceObservations.fact: The camera changes relative framing as the route advances: isolated targets are given breathing room, then the view compresses around columns, waffle hazards and stacked objects.
referenceObservations.playerEffect: The next action is staged before the knife commits; the player reads depth and height rather than only x-distance.

referenceObservations.fact: The finish camera shifts into a close, reward-oriented composition with wall, knife and pedestal occupying the same visual field.
referenceObservations.playerEffect: The final lane choice becomes an authored climax instead of a distant HUD event.

referenceObservations.fact: Camera distance and visible depth make shadows and object height meaningful; the route is not presented as a flat fixed-angle strip.
referenceObservations.playerEffect: Approach speed, obstacle scale and landing risk are perceptually legible.

oursEvidence: src/three-world-renderer.ts render() updates cameraTargetX from player.x + 255 and then reuses createCameraSpec().

src/three-presentation.ts createCameraSpec() keeps fov 24 and a fixed relative camera position/target relationship; there is no gameplay camera mode for obstacle reveal, finish close-up, yaw/pitch change or reward framing.
The default runtime has no camera shake/trauma hook tied to cut or finish events.
cameraReview.acceptance: Natural desktop and 390x844 traces must show at least traversal framing, obstacle-reveal framing and finish-wall framing, with readable knife/target relation in each mode.

commit: target centered in a readable depth frame
recovery: failure cause is local and visible

factoryControlsRequired: Blueprint must declare camera beats: traversal, reveal, pressure, finish and terminal transition; one fixed camera spec is insufficient.
Builder runtime-product gate must list the default camera controller and event wiring; POC-only camera/feel code cannot satisfy the gate.
QA must record camera mode, target object, viewport, knife relation and player-visible evidence for every named reproduction branch.
Add a realtime earnings gate requiring local delta + run total + persistent currency semantics on natural cuts and finish settlement.
Add a retention gate for failure continue/retry choices and reject debug/test controls on the default route.
Add an authored object-grammar sample across early/mid/late beats; object count alone is not variety evidence.
nextRoute: formal-fixer triage for camera state machine, default-path cut-feel/economy feedback and completion staging; separate art-direction/asset gate for object grammar.
claimBoundary: Web-lite experience retro only; native platform packaging and real-device behavior remain unverified.
